subject: body
title: Grains, Protein, Dairy
about: What the other three food groups do for the body: grains from grass plants give lasting energy, whole grains keep the whole seed, and rice, tortillas, naan and noodles are everyday grains around the world; protein builds and fixes muscles and skin (eggs, beans, fish, nuts and tofu, with beans counting twice and plant protein for families who eat no meat); and dairy brings calcium and vitamin D for bones and teeth, with fortified soy milk for kids who cannot drink cow's milk. NC 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them) and 1.NPA.1.3 (plant or animal source). Read it together; sorting foods into groups was the Food Groups level, this one is about the jobs.
tip: At dinner, point to one food and ask: is this a go food, a builder or a bone helper?

cards.q: Bread, tortillas, rice and oats all come from which kind of plant?
cards.note: Wheat, rice, oats and corn are all grasses. Their seeds are the grains we grind into flour or cook whole.

cards.q: Oatmeal, brown rice and whole wheat bread keep the whole grain seed. What are they called?
cards.note: Whole grains keep the whole seed, so they have more fiber and helpers. Try to make about half of your grains whole grains.

cards.q: Whole grain bread and rice are usually which color?
cards.note: Brown rice, brown bread, oats. A grown-up can check the label for the word whole.

cards.q: Oatmeal for breakfast is a whole grain. How long does its energy last?
cards.note: Whole grains let out their energy slowly, so you stay full and ready to learn until lunch.

cards.q: Pasta, bread and crackers are made from grains ground into a powder. What is the powder called?
cards.note: Flour is ground-up grain. Whole wheat flour keeps the whole seed.

cards.q: You scrape your knee. Which food job helps your body build new skin?
cards.note: Protein builds new skin, muscle, hair and blood. Eggs, beans, fish, meat, nuts and tofu are protein foods.

cards.q: Some families eat no meat at all. What can they eat to get plenty of protein?
cards.note: Beans, lentils, peas, tofu and nuts are plant protein foods. Vegetarians build strong muscles with them every day.

cards.q: Beans are special. They count as protein and also as which other group?
cards.note: Beans, peas and lentils are in two groups at once. They build like protein and have fiber like vegetables.

cards.q: Fish is a protein food with a special helper for which thinking part of you?
cards.note: Fish like salmon have omega-3, a helper that growing brains need. Fish is a builder food too.

cards.q: Peanut butter, nuts, beans and tofu are protein foods. Where do they come from?
cards.note: Protein does not only come from animals; plants give protein too. Check with a grown-up before sharing nuts, since some kids are allergic.

cards.q: Chicken, fish, beef and eggs are protein foods. Where do they come from?
cards.note: Farmers raise chickens and cows. Fish come from rivers, lakes and the sea.

cards.q: Milk, yogurt and cheese give you calcium. Which two hard parts does calcium make strong?
cards.note: Calcium is the hard stuff in bones and teeth. Kids need lots because bones are still growing.

cards.q: Milk has a sunshine vitamin added that helps calcium work. What is it called?
cards.note: Vitamin D helps your body use calcium. Sunshine on your skin makes some, and milk has it added.

cards.q: Some kids cannot drink cow's milk. What can they drink to get calcium instead?
cards.note: Fortified means calcium and vitamins are added. Some families use oat or almond milk with calcium added; a grown-up checks the label.

cards.q: Yogurt has friendly tiny helpers that live in your tummy. What do they help?
cards.note: Yogurt is milk with friendly bacteria added that help your tummy break food down. Pick plain or low-sugar yogurt and add fruit.

cards.q: Rice, tortillas, naan and noodles are everyday foods around the world. Which group are they all in?
cards.note: Every country has its own grain food. Rice in China, tortillas in Mexico, naan in India, pasta in Italy, injera in Ethiopia.

cards.q: Which food group is the main energy giver for running and playing?
cards.note: Grains are the go foods. Bread, rice, pasta, oats and tortillas fill your energy tank.
